Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the required multi-wake visual-evidence skill. I’ll keep all inspection and edits inside this Phase 2 workspace, then validate that exactly one candidate plus both required documentation updates are present.

The workspace confirms that visual diagnosis must precede any policy change and that only the candidate file is editable under `solver/`. I’m now reading the full required skill and the remaining workspace/guidance contract before interpreting the rollout.

I found four sampled rollouts and inherited optimizer records. The strongest scalar result is still an unstable run, so I’m treating the finite, low-load domain-exit run as the main mechanism comparison—not as a success—and checking both against the seed and immediate-instability failure.

The visual-first skill now drives the next action: I’m inspecting the common prewarm sheet, then the released sheets for the best-progress unstable controller and the low-load reversed-domain-exit controller, with the seed as the baseline.

The evidence separates two failure modes clearly: positive bearing curvature produced genuine upstream progress but escalated into joint-cap contact and catastrophic loads; reversing the curvature sign stayed numerically calm but turned the fish away and exited the downstream boundary. I’m now checking the exact observation conventions and controller contract before writing a single bounded successor.

Per the visual-first skill, I’m recording the diagnosis and falsifiable policy hypothesis before touching the candidate. The proposed successor keeps the only mechanism that made upstream progress—positive body-frame bearing curvature—but replaces its cap-hitting oscillator with the sampled radial-energy regulator and a parameter-owned soft acceleration bound.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The lesson is deliberately negative/conditional: it records that derivative and load feedback did not survive the sampled evidence, while positive bearing curvature remains only a far-field direction signal—not proof of wake entry or capture. I’m moving to contract, schema, provenance, and edit-boundary checks; no CFD will be run.

I’m invoking the configured `check-runner` as the workspace requires. It will perform the three prescribed checks independently and read-only; I’ll repair any failure it identifies and rerun the relevant checks.
